name: trust
quote: She's been through this before and will do fine.
description: Relying on a person, group, tool, or idea to support something important to you. It may be based on past experience, logic, or faith.
examples: My car has never failed to get me work before.

variations.name: social trust
variations.description: Relying on a person or group to behave in a particular and desired way.
examples: trusting your kid to finish her homework
trusting the government agency to not lose the form

variations.name: trust in a tool
variations.description: Relying on a non-living thing to be useful in accomplishing something.
examples: His trusty sword kept him safe.

variations.name: trust in an idea
variations.description: Relying on a concept to be useful in accomplishing something.
examples: He trusts the free market to be efficient.

variations.name: account of trust
variations.description: We keep an internal tally of how much a person or group has earned or spent our willingness to trust them.
examples: He normally pays me back on time.

comparisons.description: If you trust something or something without evidence, there may be an element of faith supporting the trust.
'Goodwill' is when the trust is unearned by past experience.

You do not have to be certain about something in order to make decisions assuming a positive outcome. For instance, you might give your neighbor a house key is so they can feed the fish when you're away. You're probably not 100% certain they won't snoop into your stuff, but you are certain the fish will die if they don't get fed.

Optimism focuses more on the general outcome, for example, that you have a good chance of winning the game. Trust is about specific things, for instance, trusting in your luck or strategy when playing that game.

commentaries.quote: We build inner models for how specific people and tools will behave in the world. We 'trust' one of these predictions When we feel confident enough to rely on it for something we desire. If that confidence is based on experience, it can grow and shrink over time.
Trust takes years to build, seconds to break, and forever to repair.

In a high-trust relationship, you can say the wrong thing, and people will still get your meaning. In a low-trust relationship, you can be very measured, even precise, and they’ll still misinterpret you.

conditions: Relying on a person, group, tool, or idea to support something important to you.
